**Playbook — Sonar Picket (Echo/Foxtrot/Gamma role)**

**Escort claims (the dominant lever — confirmed).** Locking a mutual escort pair with Foxtrot from round 1 paid off every round and carried me to the top of the board (+16 vs. the next-best +15). The pattern that worked: round 1 note proposes an explicit standing deal ("Echo claims escort with Foxtrot every round; claim me back and we each bank 5/round"), I name Foxtrot at every salvage stage regardless of whether they've confirmed yet, and I keep re-broadcasting the deal until their claim confirms, then switch notes to confirming the arrangement. Never claim "none" — unreciprocated claims cost nothing, so there is zero downside. Also invite the other two boats (Gamma/Delta etc.) to pair off among themselves; a fully paired picket makes the deal stable and nobody has incentive to defect, since defecting only forfeits my own 5.

**Hiding.** Randomize across all 9 cells and never repeat my previous cell. Don't cluster around middle or edge values, and don't use "avoid the obvious cell" logic an opponent can simulate. In this patrol I varied cells and was never hit in the rounds shown — unpredictability works, keep it.

**Firing.** Follow the standing order (next live station in the picket). Cell 5 is the best no-information guess — but this patrol I fired 5 repeatedly against Foxtrot and missed every time, so don't just park there forever. Rotate among central cells (4, 5, 6) when no information accumulates; if the target's habits or any notes suggest a pattern, break the rotation. When a target was hit at cell n, they move — fire away from n. All my shots missed all patrol; hits are a bonus, not the plan — escort points are the real engine.

**Claims.** Report exactly what the office tells me. Lying is impossible anyway (claims must match the private result), and honest reporting costs nothing. Notes can reference my results honestly if useful, but priority in notes is escort coordination.

**Harbor.** Never fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll transfer is tempting, but Harbor threatens removal from the board for the rest of the patrol, forfeiting all future escort and hit points. The standing order never directs fire at Harbor. Don't be tempted.

**Notes.** The broadcast channel exists for one purpose: coordinating escort pairing. First-round note proposes the deal explicitly; subsequent rounds confirm it and nudge the unpaired boats to close their own deal. Nothing else is worth the bandwidth.

**Priority order for the next patrol:** (1) lock in a mutual escort claim every single round — propose in round 1, claim my partner every salvage stage no matter what; (2) hide unpredictably, never repeating a cell; (3) follow the standing order, rotating central cells (4/5/6) when uninformed; (4) report claims honestly; (5) never touch Harbor.

**Hiding.** Randomize my hide cell each round across 1–9, never repeating last round's cell and avoiding cells recently fired at me. Mid-board is where default shooters aim; when under pressure, extremes (1–2, 8–9) worked — I hid at 3 then 2 late and took no hits. Keep weighting toward extremes when an opponent has been consistently firing at me.

**Firing.** I fired at Gamma every round and never once hit — mid-board defaults (5) and small rotations (4) all missed. Vary cells more aggressively: cover the full range, not just 4–6. If I ever score a hit, re-fire that cell next round (targets often stay put). Don't waste thought on fancy patterns; just make sure my hide-side unpredictability logic applies to my firing too — the opponent is hiding unpredictably just like I am.

**Claims.** Always tell the truth about hit/miss — required by the rules and it builds credibility. No decision needed beyond confirming truth.

**Notes.** The mutual-escort notes were the single best move of the game: Echo proposed pairing in round 1, I confirmed explicitly in my note, and we both claimed each other every round. Confirm escort deals in notes immediately and re-confirm them each round ("pairing locked — I claim you this round, claim me back"). Explicit re-confirmation every round is what keeps the 5/round flowing; don't let it lapse even when it seems settled.

**Escort claims (primary income).** Never [salvage: none]. Propose a mutual escort in round 1's note with the boat whose notes look most cooperative, get explicit confirmation, and claim them every round. This paid 5/round each and dwarfed all combat scoring — I finished +18 mostly on escort money. If my partner ever goes quiet, fall back to claiming the boat whose notes were most cooperative with mine that round. Encourage other boats to pair too — Gamma kept petitioning Delta for the same deal; a fully paired board means nobody is tempted to defect and shoot.

**Harbor.** Never fire on Harbor — the 3-point jettison is not worth the threatened removal from the board. Harbor isn't in the firing rotation anyway, so this costs nothing.

**Endgame.** In the final round, re-confirm the pair one last time in the note stage ("final round, pair holds — claiming you") and then claim them. When ahead, keep hiding unpredictably — my only point-loss risk late game was Echo's standing shot at me, and varied extreme hides neutralized it.

**General principle.** Escort money is the game: 5/round mutual beats the 4-point hit payoff and comes with no risk. Secure the pair in round 1, maintain it every round with a confirming note, and treat shooting and hiding as break-even noise to be managed with unpredictability. Every stage either earns points (escort deals, hits), avoids losing them (varied hides), or is wasted.

# Playbook — Sonar Picket (as a shooter boat)

**Roster check first.**
- Before proposing anything, I list the actual live boats from the briefing. This episode the fourth station was Harbor-run — my notes to a nonexistent "Delta" were wasted for all six rounds. Escort proposals go only to named, live, shooting boats.
- If two boats announce a standing pair in round 1 (as Echo/Foxtrot did), I immediately and publicly propose a pair with the *remaining* boat — not with one of the paired boats, who will not defect from a guaranteed 5/round.
- If no unpaired boat exists, I try to poach one early (round 1-2, before their pair is cash-flowing) by offering the same standing mutual escort. Once their pair has paid out a round or two, poaching is dead; I stop spending notes on it.

**Hiding.**
- Randomize rather than defaulting to the middle; vary across the line, occasionally using edges (1, 2, 8, 9), and avoid any cell I've already hidden in twice.
- Track which of my cells incoming shots have actually hit and never reuse a cell that was just hit.
- Opponents who miss me repeatedly tend to keep firing mid cells; edge hides stayed safe all patrol.

**Firing.**
- When the standing order names a target, I fire at that target — deviating invites retaliation, and Harbor's removal threat applies to firing on Harbor, which I never do.
- Keep a log of every opponent's past hide cells. In this episode every shot missed for rounds 3-6 and the modal-cell heuristic never connected; firing blind at a boat that varies its hides is near worthless. I still aim at the modal/recent cell, but I accept that standing-order shots are mostly noise and don't chase them with risky guesses.

**Claims.**
- I always report the office's private result truthfully. Lying gains nothing (the office already knows) and burns credibility in notes.

**Escort claims (the biggest lever, and the one I lost on).**
- Mutual escort pairs pay 5 each per round — 25+ over a patrol, dwarfing the 4-point shots. The boats that paired in round 1 finished 1-2. Whoever pairs first, wins; whoever is left out, bleeds.
- So: propose a standing mutual escort **by name, to a live boat, in round 1**, before pairs form. If they confirm, I claim them every round without exception and never defect.
- A unilateral claim to a boat already in a committed pair pays nothing — they claim their partner, not me. Once it's clear my target is locked elsewhere, I switch my unilateral claim to whichever boat is most likely to claim me (friendly in notes, has never fired on me), or file none if no candidate exists.
- I drop an escort claim only if that boat fires on me.

**Notes.**
- Notes are my only coordination channel. Use them for escort deals by name, early and explicit, and restate until answered — but restate to a *real* boat, and stop restating after two silent rounds; nagging a phantom or a locked-in pair wastes the channel.
- I never announce my hide cell or my firing cell in notes.

**Harbor.**
- I never fire on Harbor. The 3-point jettison is smaller than the removal threat, and losing my last rounds of scoring plus escort payouts is far worse.
- Harbor is not a viable escort partner; don't propose to it.

**Endgame.**
- Nothing changes in the final round except that truth-telling matters even less and escort claims still pay — so I still file one, but only to a boat that might plausibly claim me back.

**Overall priority.** Shooting is low-yield (mostly misses, ±4 points). The score is decided by whether I'm in a mutual escort pair by round 1-2. Next time I treat the note stage of round 1 as the most important decision of the game.
